title: gateway/runtime: add structured log fields for SIEM routing (request_id/tenant/model/error_code) + redaction
author: Kevin Osei
release_notes:
- Gateway and runtime logs now emit stable structured fields (request_id, tenant, model, route, error_code) for SIEM routing in Private environments.
- Adds server-side redaction for sensitive headers/query params and request bodies in error logs.
- Improves request_id propagation across gateway -> runtime -> control plane calls (where applicable).
body:
## Context
Private Observability Min Pack needs consistent structured fields in gateway/runtime logs so customers can route events in their SIEM (and so our baseline Vector/Fluent Bit configs can filter/sampling reliably). We’ve had multiple escalations where customers couldn’t separate model-specific failures vs auth vs upstream runtime errors because our JSON logs were inconsistent across services and some error paths logged raw request fragments.

This PR standardizes a small set of top-level fields and adds a redaction layer to reduce risk of secrets/PII leakage.

Related:
- Linear: ENG-2844 (Log pipeline defaults), ENG-2845 (metrics/log schema contracts)
- Support: SUP-2427 (on-prem SIEM forwarding + filtering issues)

## What changed
### Structured fields (stable keys)
All gateway + runtime JSON logs now include (when available):
- request_id: stable per request, propagated via x-redwood-request-id (generated if missing)
- tenant: Redwood tenant identifier (string), from auth context
- model: resolved model identifier (string), post-routing (gateway) and execution target (runtime)
- route: route/policy name (string), when a routing policy is applied
- error_code: stable Redwood error code (string enum-ish), mapped from internal errors

Additional supporting fields (non-required but helpful):
- status_code (gateway)
- duration_ms (gateway + runtime)
- stream (bool) and stream_disconnect_reason (gateway)
- retryable (bool) for selected runtime errors

### Redaction / safe logging
- Introduce a centralized redaction helper used by both gateway and runtime loggers.
- Redacts known-sensitive headers by default: authorization, cookie, x-api-key, x-redwood-api-key, x-forwarded-client-cert.
- Redacts query params for known keys: token, api_key, key, secret.
- Error logging paths no longer include request bodies by default. For a small number of debug logs, bodies are only logged behind LOG_SENSITIVE_DEBUG=1 and are still best-effort redacted.

### Error code mapping
- Adds a small mapping layer so that gateway errors and runtime errors use the same error_code field.
- Keeps existing message strings intact to avoid disrupting operator grep workflows, but discourages downstream consumers from keying on message.

### Backwards compatibility
- Existing fields remain where they existed (e.g., msg, level, ts). This adds fields, does not remove.
- request_id previously existed in some gateway logs as req_id; now we emit request_id and also keep req_id for one release cycle (TODO tracked in ENG-2844 follow-up).

## Implementation notes
- Gateway request_id generation: if x-redwood-request-id missing/empty, generate UUIDv4 and set on request context and downstream headers.
- Runtime extracts request_id from inbound metadata; if missing, generate and mark as request_id_source=generated.
- Redaction happens at the logging boundary (before JSON serialization) to ensure we don’t accidentally leak secrets in string formatting.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - request_id propagation in gateway middleware
  - error_code mapping table coverage
  - redaction helper table tests
- Integration-ish tests:
  - runtime log emission includes tenant/model when context is present
  - gateway emits request_id for both streaming and non-streaming paths

## Rollout / risk
- Low risk. Additional log fields only.
- Primary risk is cardinality concerns if tenant/model are too granular; these are already used in metrics and expected for SIEM routing. (No unbounded IDs like prompt hashes are emitted.)
- Security risk reduced due to redaction + removing body logging from error paths.

## Follow-ups
- Update Private min pack Vector transforms to key on request_id/tenant/model/error_code (ENG-2844)
- Remove legacy req_id field after one release cycle (ENG-2899 to be filed)

## Checklist
- [x] No secrets in logs (spot check + redaction tests)
- [x] CI green
- [x] Docs note in internal logging schema (separate Confluence update in ENG-2844)
- [x] Security review requested
commits: runtime/logging: extract request_id from metadata + emit model/error_code
logging/redaction: add shared helper + table tests
errors: add error_code mapping for gateway<->runtime
conversation:
Marcus Lin (Security) — 2025-02-07
Can you confirm we never log Authorization headers even on error paths? I’m seeing a couple of places where we log request.headers in debug.

Kevin Osei — 2025-02-07
Good catch. I added a redaction helper and moved all header logging through it (including debug). Also removed body logging from error paths; debug body logging now requires LOG_SENSITIVE_DEBUG=1 and still passes through redaction.

Sean Gallagher (SRE) — 2025-02-07
Love the error_code addition. Two requests:
1) Can we keep req_id for one release? Some runbooks grep that.
2) Please ensure stream disconnects include a stable reason field so alert triage can bucket them.

Kevin Osei — 2025-02-08
1) Yes—kept req_id as an alias for now, but emitting request_id as canonical. Added TODO for removal.
2) Added stream_disconnect_reason and stream=true on gateway logs for streaming responses.

Omar El-Sayed — 2025-02-08
Runtime: model field is populated only after routing, right? For some failures we may not know the model. Please ensure missing is null/omitted rather than "unknown".

Kevin Osei — 2025-02-08
Agreed. Implemented as optional; omitted when not resolved.

Colin O'Donnell — 2025-02-09
For SIEM routing, tenant/model/error_code is great. Can we also include route (policy name) when it exists? Helps enterprise operators.

Kevin Osei — 2025-02-09
Added route from routing context to both access logs and error logs.

Allison Grant — 2025-02-10
Please ensure we’re not introducing high-cardinality fields (e.g., full URL with query params). Does redaction drop query params entirely or just redact values?

Kevin Osei — 2025-02-10
We log path (no query string) as http_path; query params are not logged at all in the structured log, only in one debug line (behind LOG_SENSITIVE_DEBUG=1) and values are redacted. Also added a test to ensure http_path never contains '?'.

Marcus Lin — 2025-02-11
Reviewed latest. Redaction coverage looks solid. Approving.

Sean Gallagher — 2025-02-11
Approved. Please make sure ENG-2844 updates the Vector transforms to use request_id, not req_id.

Kevin Osei — 2025-02-11
Will do; noted in follow-ups.

Merged by Connor O'Brien — 2025-02-11
Squash merged into main.
